evidence:
tests/test_native_open_depth.py:266-269 `if proc.poll() is None:
                # The connection closed and the owner lives (QUIT): reconnect.
                print("OPEN-DEPTH {} {} SERVED {} (closed) seconds={:.1f}".format(` with only owner deaths appended to `deaths`, and :202 `self.assertEqual([(t, e) for t, e, _ in self.deaths], [], ...)`
fix: Record a non-QUIT EOF or OSError against a live owner as a failure (a `drops` list asserted empty, like `deaths`). At least require the first line to be a known reply code for that command.

reviewer: test_native_open_depth.py:241-276: an EOF or OSError on any command, with the owner alive, prints '(closed)' and reconnects. Only owner deaths are recorded, and :202 asserts only that list. Reply codes are printed, never asserted. The test's stated scope is 'commands or reports that stopped the owner' (plus open timing), so this is a weak test, not a hidden failure.
scenario: At a deep store, OVER/LISTGROUP/HDR overrun a work bound and the owner closes the session (EOF) instead of answering. Or the client's 1800 s read times out with OSError while the owner is still alive. Either way run() prints `(closed)`, reconnects and moves on. The test asserts only that the owner did not die, so a command that never returns a reply at depth passes. The comment admits this is meant only for QUIT, but it applies to every command. Reply codes are not checked either, so a 503 for every command passes.
title: The open-depth sweep counts any connection the server drops while still alive as success
